title: Area of a Rectangle as a Function of Its Width
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: A rectangle has fixed perimeter $20$ units. Writing its width as $x$, express the enclosed area $A$ as a function of $x$ and give the physically meaningful domain.

steps.title: Extract the Length from the Perimeter
steps.explanation: Half the perimeter is $10$, so width plus length equals $10$ and the length must be $10-x$.
steps.why: Perimeter constraints let one dimension eliminate the other.

steps.title: Multiply Dimensions for the Area Model
steps.explanation: Area is width times length, producing the quadratic model $A(x)=x(10-x)=10x-x^{2}$.
steps.why: The product of the two dependent dimensions yields a single-variable function.

steps.title: Impose Physical Bounds on x
steps.explanation: Both dimensions must be strictly positive, which forces $x$ into the open interval $(0,10)$.
steps.why: Degenerate rectangles (zero width or zero length) are excluded from the geometric domain.
